turns.utterance: Please complete the following checks: First, inspect the magazine pockets for any deformation, cracking, or swarf accumulation. Next, check the gripper arm fingers for bending, cracking, or worn contact faces. Finally, inspect the magazine drive mechanism for seized bearings or loose fasteners.

turns.utterance: Do you see any magazine deformation, cracked pockets, or broken gripper fingers?

turns.utterance: Is the gripper finger spread within retention force tolerance?

turns.utterance: Is the locating pin diameter within H6/h5 fit tolerance?

turns.utterance: Is the tool retention force within rated range for all tested pockets?

turns.utterance: No, the pull gauge readings are coming in below the minimum specification. The retention force is insufficient.

turns.utterance: Adjust the drawbar clamping pressure or replace the Belleville washers as needed.

turns.utterance: Perform a secondary drawbar overhaul. Extend the drawbar to expose the disc spring stack and inspect each spring for cracking, deformation, or dimensional issues. Replace the complete spring stack with new springs from the correct part number kit, then reset the drawbar preload to specification using a compression gauge.

ground_truth.node_text: Secondary drawbar overhaul: extend the drawbar to expose the disc spring stack and inspect each spring for cracking, deformation, or dimensional out of specification. Replace the complete spring stack with new springs from the correct part number kit. Reset the drawbar preload to the specification value using a compression gauge before returning to the tool retention force measurement step.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Drawbar overhaul complete. Found some deformed springs in the stack. Replaced with new springs and reset the preload.

ground_truth.node_text: Secondary drawbar overhaul: extend the drawbar to expose the disc spring stack and inspect each spring for cracking, deformation, or dimensional out of specification. turns.utterance: Reverify the tool retention force after the overhaul. Is it now within specification?

turns.utterance: Access the alarm log and filter by tool changer related alarm codes. Record the tool number, pocket number, and alarm description. Check whether the alarm pattern correlates with a specific pocket or tool.

turns.utterance: I've pulled the alarm log. Both faults were related to pocket three, looks like a positioning issue on that specific pocket.

turns.utterance: Reverify the tool changer cycle after your fault investigation. Does it now complete successfully?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, after addressing the pocket three alignment, all ten cycles completed without any faults.

ground_truth.node_text: Reverify tool changer cycle after fault investigation

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the tool length measurement within plus or minus 0.01 millimeters of the stored offset?

turns.utterance: Yes, the measured offset matches the stored value within tolerance.

ground_truth.node_text: Tool length measurement within ±0.01 mm of stored offset?

turns.utterance: Have all lubrication points been serviced per specification?

turns.utterance: Yes, I've applied grease to all cam follower and guide rail points and cycled the arm to distribute it.

ground_truth.node_text: All lubrication points serviced per specification?

turns.utterance: Log all tool changer measurements and update the service record.

turns.utterance: All measurements logged and service record updated in the system.
